# speexdsp, vendored

What this is, why it is here as source rather than as a library, and how to
check it has not been touched.

## What it does

speexdsp cleans up microphone sound before it is sent: echo cancellation,
noise suppression, automatic gain and voice detection. None of that is
coding, and Opus does none of it. A call that hands the microphone straight
to the encoder sends the far end its own voice back a moment later.

Schultz reaches it through `schultz_voice.h`. Nothing outside
`schultz_voice.c` includes a speexdsp header.

## Why it is compiled in

Two reasons, and the second is the one that decided it.

libunibreak is vendored this way because it is a small, self-contained C
library with no configuration worth having. speexdsp is the same shape:
eleven C files, five public headers, no dependencies.

And it is the only library here that is autotools only. Everything else
builds with cmake, and `scripts/build_deps.sh` has no autotools path and no
host triple in its target files to give one. Adding both, for eleven files
that compile with no flags, would be more moving parts than the thing it
builds.

## The configuration

`config.h` in this directory is what speexdsp's `configure` would have
written, written by hand. It says three things:

- `FLOATING_POINT`. Every target Schultz builds for has a floating point
  unit. The fixed point build exists for chips that do not.
- `USE_KISS_FFT`. The FFT that ships with speexdsp. The alternatives are FFTW
  and Intel's MKL, each a separate dependency with a separate licence.
- `EXPORT` as nothing. These symbols do not leave the library; Schultz
  exports `schultz_*` and nothing else.

`include/speex/speexdsp_config_types.h` is likewise generated by configure
from a `.in`, and is written out here as the four `<stdint.h>` types it
always resolves to on a C99 compiler.

Those three files are the only things in this directory that are not upstream
byte for byte. `scripts/check_vendored.sh` checks the rest.

## The version

speexdsp 1.2.1, from the release tarball at
`downloads.xiph.org/releases/speex/`, pinned and hashed in
`scripts/versions.sh` like every other dependency.

Not the archive gitlab.xiph.org generates on demand: an archive a server
builds when asked is not a thing that can be pinned, which is the same reason
libyuv was rejected. See `design/video-design.md`.
